title: CORRECTION: cliffs = the biome's curved Wang tile EXTRUDED tall (corners/edges/filler + sub-variants), darker sides — replace the S293 separate cliff-face box system
intent: S293 (GDP-2026-06-04-001) built a SEPARATE cliff-face system (cliff-grass/cliff-stone biomes, flat vertical face meshes, corner caps, strata). After two fix/polish rounds it still looks wrong: raised plateaus are coloured CUBES with hard square edges, while flat grass/stone are organic curved tiles. The plateau top does NOT autotile — no corner/edge/filler shapes. The correct, far simpler design (user call 2026-06-04): a cliff is just the SAME biome tile as flat ground — the curved-outline Wang mesh with its corner/edge/strip/T/filler shapes AND 3 sub-variants — EXTRUDED to the cell's height, with the side walls painted in the biome's colour but darker (vertical gradient, darkest at the base = contact shadow). No separate cliff biomes, no face Wang resolver, no corner caps, no pillar boxes. A grass plateau is a grass tile that's tall; a stone plateau is a tall stone tile. The top edge curves and corners exactly like the flat island, so plateaus stop reading as cubes.
rationale: User 2026-06-04: 'утесы покрашены но остаются кубами, а должны иметь также угловые и другие типы тайлов как камень или трава' + 'почему утесы не сделать также как stones но выше и покрасить боковые грани как верх но темнее?'. The biome tile (grass-variants assembleGeometry) ALREADY extrudes darker side faces (sideCol = GRASS_SHADOW) — they're just thin (0.20). Making them tall IS the cliff. This deletes a whole subsystem (cliff-face-variants.ts) and reuses the curved-tile work from GDP-2026-06-04-003/004. Camera is orthographic pitched −55° (angled top-down): the most-visible line is the TOP EDGE, so an organic curved top rim + a simple darker vertical wall reads as a cliff; elaborate face geometry was invisible/artefacting and is why S293 thrashed.
acceptanceHints: READ FIRST: docs/game-design/tile-edge-library-design.md §8 (REWRITTEN for this approach), grass-variants.ts assembleGeometry (the biome tile already extrudes darker sides — just thin), bootstrap-helpers.ts (heightmap.pillar boxes — to be removed for biome cells).
DELETE the S293 separate cliff-face system

SALVAGE FIRST — keep the side-wall colour gradient the dev built (user likes it): before deleting cliff-face-variants.ts, lift out its per-biome vertical colour ramps and KEEP them as the side-wall gradient of the tall tile (see §A). Stone ramp: STONE_LIGHT #8f897b → STONE_MID #565145 → STONE_DARK #33302a → STONE_SHADOW #19170f. Grass-topped soil ramp: GRASS crown #5aa838 → SOIL_LIGHT #9a6f3e → SOIL_MID #5e3f20 → dark #241a0e. These are the gradients to preserve.

Then remove: examples/kaboom-crew/src/blocks/cliff-face-variants.ts (buildCliffFace / buildCliffCorner / cliffVariant), its builder registrations in register-block-builders.ts, the cliff-grass/cliff-stone biomes, and the cliff-face spawner/Wang resolver. Keep the gameplay cliff RULES (blast-stop, grid-mover block, step-jump) — those are in blast/grid systems, not the renderer; do not touch them.

Remove the heightmap.pillar.* box spawns (bootstrap-helpers.ts) for cells that carry a biome overlay — the tall biome tile becomes the visible plateau. (Keep a neutral fallback pillar only for raised cells with NO terrainmap biome, e.g. debug heightmaps.)
A. THE TILE GAINS A HEIGHT — tall biome tile = cliff
Extend the biome tile builders (grass/stone/path/dirt — the GDP-2026-06-04-003/004 buildXxxShape) with a height parameter:
buildGrassShape(shape, sub, heightCells = 0)  // 0 = flat overlay (current); >0 = plateau
TOP face: same curved Wang outline + sub-variant + (for grass) flat top, placed at Y = heightCells (the plateau surface).
SIDE faces: extrude from the top outline DOWN to Y = 0 (full drop), exactly the existing side-face loop in assembleGeometry but with height = heightCells instead of the thin 0.20.

SIDE colour: KEEP the multi-stop vertical gradient the dev built (user explicitly likes the stone + grass-topped cliff gradients) — port the salvaged ramps as the side-wall colour: stone walls use the STONE_LIGHT→MID→DARK→SHADOW ramp; grass-topped walls use the GRASS-crown→SOIL_LIGHT→MID→dark ramp; path/dirt walls use an equivalent ramp built from their own palette (top tint at the crown darkening to a near-black contact shadow at the base). Map gradient position v = 0 (base) … 1 (top of wall). This is the 'paint the sides like the top but darker' look, with the nice weathered-crown→shadowed-base falloff preserved.
Overhang: the top-edge overhang (grass lip) now curls over the tall drop — this reads correctly because it sits at the TOP silhouette (the −55° camera sees it as a rim), NOT on the face. Keep it.
B. PLATEAU AUTOTILING — corners/edges come from the SAME Wang resolver
A raised cell's Wang bitmask is computed over its cardinal neighbours that are ALSO raised to the SAME height AND the same biome:
neighbour raised+same → that edge is FLUSH (plateau continues; tiles merge seamlessly).
neighbour lower / different / void → that edge is OPEN (curved outline + overhang + the tall dark side shows there — this is the cliff drop).

Result: a plateau gets Shape A/B/C/D/E/F exactly like a flat island — rounded convex corners (Shape C), curved edges (Shape B), flush interior (Shape F). NO square cubes, NO corner caps (the curved corner tile + its dark side IS the cliff corner).
Sub-variant per raised cell via the existing per-cell hash → adjacent plateau corners/edges differ (not stamped).
delta ≥ 2: same tile, taller extrusion. Multi-level plateaus stack naturally.
C. WHAT STAYS

C-1 seam-pin, C-3 split-normals, C-4 corner-rounding (GDP-2026-06-04-003/006) apply unchanged — the tall tile is the same mesh with a deeper side. Gameplay cliff rules unchanged. Theme palette (S172) drives both top + darkened side.
D. TESTS
buildGrassShape('A', 0, 0): flat overlay — side height ≈ 0.20 (unchanged regression).
buildGrassShape('A', 0, 2): plateau — boundingBox Y span ≈ 2.0; top face at Y≈2; side faces reach Y=0.
buildGrassShape('C', 0, 2): tall corner tile — top outline has the rounded convex corner (C-4), side faces present on the open edges. (Plateau corner is curved, not square.)

Side colour gradient: sampled side-face vertex colours form a vertical ramp — crown (top) is the brightest darkened tint, base is markedly darker (near contact-shadow); luminance(top-of-wall) > luminance(base). Confirms the dev's gradient is preserved, not a flat single darken.
Plateau Wang: a 3×3 block of same-height same-biome raised cells → centre cell is Shape F (flush, no exposed side), perimeter cells are edge/corner shapes with exposed dark sides.
No cliff-face-variants symbols remain (buildCliffFace/buildCliffCorner deleted; no import references).
Existing grass/stone/path/dirt flat-tile tests still pass.
E. VISUAL QA (the user's actual ask)
Load all-biomes-demo / a height-varied arena. Top-down + low-angle (the −55° game camera) screenshots.
PASS:
Plateaus have ORGANIC curved top edges + rounded corners — identical autotiling to flat grass/stone, just raised. No square cubes.
Side walls keep the dev's nice vertical gradient — weathered brighter crown fading to a deep shadowed base (the stone + grass-topped cliff gradients the user liked), in the biome's colour family.
A grass plateau reads as grass on top; a stone plateau as stone — same biome top as the equivalent flat tile.
Adjacent same-height cells merge into one plateau with no inter-cell gaps or seams; the drop-off edge curves.
Plateau corners vary (sub-variants) — not all identical.
FAIL (any → reject):
Plateau tops are square boxes / hard grid edges (still cubes — Wang not applied to raised cells).
A separate flat cliff-face mesh or corner-cap wedge is visible.
Side walls are the same brightness as the top (no darkening) or a different hue than the biome.
Visible gaps/cracks between adjacent plateau cells.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Per-biome side texture detail beyond the dark gradient (strata, cracks) — defer; the dark wall is enough.
Cliff-specific gameplay changes (rules already shipped).
Surface-generator elevation handoff (Phase 2 of GDP-2026-06-04-008 consumes this once it lands).
